audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant, final stress (final stress)' rests on Wright 2009, the sole grammar sketch of Anu-Hkongso and the only descriptive work Glottolog lists; the deciding sentence is verbatim at sec. 2.3.2 p. 30. The one later source, Wright's 2020/2022 JIPA Illustration (downloaded now, open from Cambridge Core), independently restates iambic minor+major word rhythm with reduced non-final syllables and a full 'major ultimate syllable', backed by duration measurements, so nothing suggests the classification is wrong. Weaknesses are bookkeeping, not substance: the record held no file and its grade field is blank; both PDFs are now under Action: register the held thesis, add the JIPA paper as corroborating citation, and set the strength of the evidence accordingly. sources.quote: p. 531-2: 'Khongso exhibits a rhythmic pattern consisting of combinations of minor and major syllables in an iambic pattern (unstressed-stressed)... Initial elements of polysyllabic constructions tend to be shorter'; 'Other polysyllabic words, such as trisyllabic words... contain reduced syllables followed by a major ultimate syllable'; minor syllables carry only /ə/ or a syllabic nasal and a level mid tone; duration regression shows minor syllables (mean 0.10-0.11 s) significantly shorter than major syllables.
